record.title: Lovász conjecture
record.statement:
Call a finite simple graph
$\Gamma$ *vertex-transitive* if its automorphism group acts transitively on $V(\Gamma)$,
and call a cycle in
$\Gamma$ *Hamiltonian* if it passes through every vertex of $\Gamma$ exactly
once.

For a cubic graph $X$ (every vertex of degree $3$), let
$T(X)$ denote the *triangle replacement* of $X$: the vertex set of
$T(X)$ is the set of pairs $(v,e)$ with $v\in V(X)$, $e\in E(X)$ and
$v$ an endpoint of $e$; two such pairs $(v,e)$ and $(w,f)$ are adjacent in
$T(X)$ if either $v=w$ and $e\neq f$ (so the three pairs at each vertex of
$X$ form a triangle), or $e=f$ and $v\neq w$.

Let $P$ be the Petersen graph, i.e. the graph whose vertices are the $2$-element
subsets of $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, two such subsets being adjacent when they are
disjoint.

Let $C$ be the Coxeter graph, i.e. the graph on the $28$ vertices

$$
\{a_i,\;b_i,\;c_i,\;v_i \;:\; i\in\mathbb{Z}_7\}
$$

with edges $a_i a_{i+1}$, $b_i b_{i+2}$, $c_i c_{i+3}$, and $v_i a_i$,
$v_i b_i$, $v_i c_i$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}_7$.

Then every finite connected vertex-transitive graph contains a Hamiltonian
cycle, with the exception of exactly five graphs up to isomorphism, namely

$$
K_2,\quad P,\quad C,\quad T(P),\quad T(C),
$$

each of which is finite, connected and vertex-transitive, contains a Hamiltonian
path, and contains no Hamiltonian cycle.
record.source_name: Wikipedia
record.references: 1. Wikipedia, [Lovász conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lov%C3%A1sz_conjecture), the article this problem comes from.

record.title: Generating-function conjecture for greedy (m,r)-Tamari intervals
record.statement:
For integers $m\geq 1$ and $1\leq r\leq m-1$, let $d53c^{(m,r)}_n$ be the set of greedy $(m,r)$-Tamari intervals of size $n$, and let

$$
F_{d53c^{(m,r)}}(t,x)=d53c_{d53c^{(m,r)}}(t,x;p_1,p_2,\ldots)
$$

be their generating function with the weights defined in the source. Let $\Omega$ denote the operator used in the source, acting on the generating functions as indicated by the displayed identities. **Generating-function conjecture for greedy $(m,r)$-Tamari intervals.** For $1\leq r\leq m-1$,

$$
F_{d53c^{(m,r)}}(t,x)=\bigl(F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)+\Omega\bigr)^{r+1}(1).
$$

For $r=0$,

$$
F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)=1+xt\bigl(F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)+\Omega\bigr)^{m+1}(1).
$$

Equivalently, for $0\leq r\leq m-2$,

$$
F_{d53c^{(m,r+1)}}(t,x)=\bigl(F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)+\Omega\bigr)F_{d53c^{(m,r)}}(t,x),
$$

and

$$
F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)=1+xt\bigl(F_{d53c^{(m,0)}}(t,x)+\Omega\bigr)F_{d53c^{(m,m-1)}}(t,x).
$$

These identities are conjectured from numerical computation and describe the generating functions of the greedy $(m,r)$-Tamari intervals.
record.source_name: Philippe Biane and Wenjie Fang, “Decomposition of Greedy Tamari Intervals and Bipartite Planar Maps”, arXiv:2607.01206 (2026).
record.references:
**10 papers in this index state this conjecture** (1998–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2507.16908](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16908), [arXiv:2504.06466](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06466), [arXiv:2401.04026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04026), [arXiv:2112.15081](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.15081), [arXiv:1809.03123](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03123), [arXiv:1411.6606](https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.6606), [arXiv:1108.2859](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.2859), [arXiv:math/9806086](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9806086), [arXiv:math/9803091](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9803091).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

record.title: PSPACE-completeness conjecture for unrestricted graph Ramsey games
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $A$ be the achievement graph, with no precolored red or green edges, denoted by $(G,A,\{\},\{\})$. **Unrestricted graph Ramsey-game conjecture.** Graph Ramsey games played on $(G,A,\{\},\{\})$ are ${\bf PSPACE}$-complete. The conjecture concerns the complexity of deciding whether the first player has a forced win from the uncolored graph, which is not implied by PSPACE-completeness for arbitrary positions; tractable subcases provide contrary evidence for some restricted families.
record.source_name: Wolfgang Slany, “Graph Ramsey games”, arXiv:cs/9911004 (1999).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9911004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 1999).

record.title: PSPACE-completeness conjecture for symmetric binary graph Ramsey avoidance games
record.statement: Let $K_k$ and $K_n$ be complete graphs, let $E^r$ and $E^g$ be precolored red and green edge sets, and let $\mathrm{Ramsey}(n,n)$ denote the classic symmetric binary Ramsey number. **Classic Ramsey-number avoidance conjecture.** Graph Ramsey avoidance games played on $(K_k,K_n,E^r,E^g)$ where $k\geq\mathrm{Ramsey}(n,n)$ are ${\bf PSPACE}$-complete. The conjecture restricts avoidance games to complete host graphs whose order is at least the corresponding symmetric binary Ramsey number; the paper presents these games as difficult, but supplies no resolution of the conjecture.

record.references:

record.title: The uniquely list chromatic number bound and equality characterization
record.statement:
For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $k$, let $\chi_u(G,k)$ be the minimum number $t$ such that $G$ is uniquely $(k,t)$-list colorable, and let $\chi_u(G)=\max_{k\geqslant 1}\chi_u(G,k)$. Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree of $G$. **The uniquely list chromatic number conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\chi_u(G)\leqslant\Delta(G)+1,
$$

and equality holds if and only if $G$ is either a complete graph or an odd cycle. This extends the result established in the paper for uniquely $2$-list colorable graphs; the conjecture proposes the corresponding bound for all positive integers $k$, together with a characterization of the equality cases.
record.source_name: Y. G. Ganjali, M. Ghebleh, H. Hajiabolhassan, M. Mirzazadeh and B. S. Sadjad, “Uniquely 2-List Colorable Graphs”, arXiv:math/9906187 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9906187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 1999).

record.title: Erdős Problem #777 — Comparable pairs in a family of subsets
record.statement: For a family $\mathcal F$ of $m$ subsets of $[n]$, join two members when one contains the other. If $\varepsilon>0$ and $m\leq(2-\varepsilon)2^{n/2}$, must there be fewer than $2^n$ comparable pairs? If there are at least $cm^2$ comparable pairs, must $m=O_c(2^{n/2})$? Finally, for every $\varepsilon>0$, is there $\delta>0$ such that more than $m^{2-\delta}$ comparable pairs imply $m<(2+\varepsilon)^{n/2}$?
